# Abstract

Stable isotope analysis is widely used to investigate elasmobranch trophic ecology, but processes like lipid and urea extraction can alter isotopic values, limiting comparisons among studies.
We evaluated two extraction protocols in two vulnerable batoid species, the eagle ray (*Myliobatis aquila*) and bull ray (*Aetomylaeus bovinus*), which are rarely available for study.
The extraction method significantly affected δ¹⁵N in *M. aquila*, but not in *A. bovinus*, whereas δ¹³C was not significantly affected in either species.
These findings highlight the importance of considering extraction procedures when interpreting stable isotope data in batoids.

siaBIO = read.csv("Rays_SIA.csv")

siaBIO$Method = factor(siaBIO$Method, levels = c("Natural", "Chloroform_Methanol ", "Petroleum Ether" ))

## Dry mass loss (%)

The initial and final dry weights were recorded to calculate the percentage of dry mass loss during extraction as follows: [dry]{.underline} mass loss (%) = [(initial dry weight − final dry weight) / initial dry weight] × 100. This measure quantifies the overall loss of dry mass during treatment and does not distinguish between lipids, urea, and other potentially extracted compounds.

Dry mass loss and C:N ratios were compared using two-way analyses of variance (ANOVA), with extraction method (Natural, CM and PE) and species as fixed factors, including their interaction (Method ×
Species).

```{r dry mass loss, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

siaBIO <- siaBIO |> 
  mutate(mloss = (Initial_dry_weight- Final_dry_weight)/Initial_dry_weight,
         mloss_perc = mloss*100) 

stat.test <- siaBIO |>
  filter(Method != "Natural") |> 
  group_by(Method) |>
  anova_test(mloss_perc ~ Species) 

# Confronti post-hoc
tukey <- siaBIO |>
  filter(Method != "Natural") |>
  group_by(Method) |>
  tukey_hsd(mloss_perc ~ Species) |>
  add_xy_position(x = "Species")

# Boxplot con significatività
siaBIO |> 
filter(Method != "Natural") |>
ggplot(aes(x = Species, y = mloss_perc)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ Method) +
  stat_pvalue_manual(
    tukey,
    label = "p.adj.signif",
    tip.length = 0.01,
    hide.ns = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_classic()
  
  



kable(siaBIO |> 
filter(Method != "Natural") |>   group_by(Species,Method) |> 
summarise(mean_mloss = round(mean(mloss_perc),2),
            sd_mloss = round(sd(mloss_perc),2)))


```

```{r C/N analysis, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

kable(siaBIO %>% 
  group_by(Method,Species) %>% 
  summarise(CNratio_mean = mean(CNratio), sd = sd(CNratio)))

my_comparisons <- list(c("Natural", "Chloroform_Methanol"), c("Chloroform_Methanol", "Petroleum Ether"), c("Natural", "Petroleum Ether"))

ggboxplot(siaBIO, x = "Method", y = "CNratio",
          color = "Method", palette = "jco", add = "jitter") +
  rotate_x_text(45)+
  stat_compare_means() +
  facet_wrap(~ Species)

siaBIO$Method <- factor(siaBIO$Method)
siaBIO$Species <- factor(siaBIO$Species)

mod <- aov(CNratio ~ Method * Species, data = siaBIO)

tab <- as.data.frame(summary(mod)[[1]])

kable(tab,
      caption = "ANOVA",
      digits = 3)
```

# SIA analysis

Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) were fitted to assess the effects of species, extraction method (PE and CM), and their interaction on δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N values, including individuals as a random intercept to account for non-independence among observations.
Separate models were also fitted for each isotope and species, including extraction method as a fixed effect and individual identity as a random effect to account for repeated measurements across extraction treatments.
Post-hoc pairwise comparisons were performed to investigate differences between species and extraction methods.

```{r sia analysis, fig.width= 9, fig.height= 8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

summ_statsN <- siaBIO %>%
  group_by(Species,Method) %>%
  summarise(mean=round(mean(dNrec), 2), 
            sd= round(sd(dNrec),2), 
            Q3= round(quantile(dNrec, 0.75), 2),.groups = 'drop')
 
kable(summ_statsN)

 summ_statsC <- siaBIO %>%
  group_by(Species, Method) %>%
  summarise(mean= round(mean(dCrec), 2), 
            sd= round(sd(dCrec), 2), 
            Q1= round(quantile(dCrec, 0.25), 2),.groups = 'drop')
 
 kable(summ_statsC)
 
```

### Effect of extraction methods on δ¹³C values in all species

```{r LMM all species d13C, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

siaBIO_sub <- siaBIO |>
  filter(Method != "Natural") |>
  mutate(
    Species = factor(Species,
                     levels = c("Ma", "Ab")),
    Method = factor(Method,
                    levels = c("Petroleum Ether", "Chloroform_Methanol "))
  )

mod_d13C_tratt <- lmer(
  dCrec ~ Species * Method + (1 | ID_new),
  data = siaBIO_sub
)

# tab_model(

#

#   digits.p = 3,
#   file = "Paper/Results/tab1_all species.doc"
# )

tab <- tidy(mod_d13C_tratt, effects = "fixed")


kable(tab, caption = "LMM", digits = 3)
```

### Effect of extraction methods on δ¹³C values in *Myliobatis aquila*

The LMM does not show a significant effect of extraction method on δ¹³C (ANOVA: p = 0.18).
Although the chloroform/methanol treatment shows a tendency toward more negative values compared to natural samples, post-hoc comparisons are not significant.

```{r LMM Myliobatis d13C, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
SIA_Ma = siaBIO %>% filter(Species == "Ma")

mod_d13C_tratt <- lmer(dCrec ~ Method + (1 | ID_new), data = SIA_Ma)

emmeans_d13C <- emmeans(mod_d13C_tratt, ~ Method)

```

```{r table models d13C Ma, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# tab_model(mod_d13C_tratt, 
#           title = "Table 1: Results of the mixed model for δ¹³C (Ma species)",
#           dv.labels = "δ¹³C",
#           string.p = "p-value",
#           file = "Paper/Results/tab1_new.doc")
tab <- tidy(mod_d13C_tratt, effects = "fixed")


kable(tab, caption = "LMM", digits = 3)
```

```{r table models d13C2 Ma, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

anova_res <- as.data.frame(anova(mod_d13C_tratt))
kable(anova_res, caption = "ANOVA test (Type III) for the effect of the Method", digits = 3) 

pairs_df <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans_d13C, adjust = "tukey"))

kable(pairs_df, caption = "Post-hoc comparisons (Tukey) between sampling methods") 
```

### Effect of extraction methods on δ¹⁵N values in *Myliobatis aquila*

The extraction method has a significant effect on δ¹⁵N (p = 0.017).
Specifically, chloroform/methanol treatment causes a significant increase in δ¹⁵N compared to natural samples.
Petroleum ether does not differ significantly from untreated samples.

```{r lMM myliobatis d15N, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
mod_d15N_tratt <- lmer(dNrec ~ Method + (1 | ID_new), data = SIA_Ma)
emmeans_d15N <- emmeans(mod_d15N_tratt, ~ Method)

```

```{r table models d15N Ma, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# tab_model(mod_d15N_tratt, 
#           title = "Table 4: Results of the mixed model for δ¹⁵N (Ma species)",
#           dv.labels = "δ¹⁵N",
#           string.p = "p-value",
#           file = "Paper/Results/tab4.doc")

tab <- tidy(mod_d15N_tratt, effects = "fixed")


kable(tab, caption = "LMM", digits = 3)
```

```{r table models d15N2 Ma, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
anova_res <- as.data.frame(anova(mod_d15N_tratt))
kable(anova_res, caption = "ANOVA test (Type III) for the effect of the Method", digits = 3) 

pairs_df <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans_d15N, adjust = "tukey"))

kable(pairs_df, caption = "Post-hoc comparisons (Tukey) between sampling methods") 
```

### Effect of extraction methods on δ¹³C values in *Aetomylaeus bovinus*

The model shows a marginal effect of extraction method on δ¹³C (p = 0.066).
The comparison between chloroform/methanol and petroleum ether suggests a potential difference, but it is not significant after correction for multiple comparisons.

```{r LMM Aetomylaeus d13C, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
SIA_Ab = siaBIO %>% filter(Species == "Ab")

mod_d13C_tratt <- lmer(dCrec ~ Method + (1 | ID_new), data = SIA_Ab)
emmeans_d13C <- emmeans(mod_d13C_tratt, ~ Method)

```

```{r table model d13C Ab, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# tab_model(mod_d13C_tratt, 
#           title = "Results of the mixed model for δ¹³C (Ab species)",
#           dv.labels = "δ¹³C",
#           string.p = "p-value",
#           file = "Paper/Results/tab7.doc")

tab <- tidy(mod_d13C_tratt, effects = "fixed")


kable(tab, caption = "LMM", digits = 3)
```

```{r table model d13C2 Ab, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
anova_res <- as.data.frame(anova(mod_d13C_tratt))
kable(anova_res, caption = "ANOVA test (Type III) for the effect of the Method", digits = 3)

pairs_df <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans_d13C, adjust = "tukey"))

kable(pairs_df, caption = "Post-hoc comparisons (Tukey) between sampling methods") 
```

### Effect of extraction methods on "δ¹⁵N" values in *Aetomylaeus bovinus*

The extraction method has no significant effect on δ¹⁵N (p = 0.40).
Values are consistent across the three treatments.

```{r Aetomylaeus d15N, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
mod_d15N_tratt <- lmer(dNrec ~ Method + (1 | ID_new), data = SIA_Ab)
emmeans_d15N <- emmeans(mod_d15N_tratt, ~ Method)
```
